subject: Audit sprint proposal & hosting decision — CardioCorp
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardiocorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Audit sprint proposal & hosting decision — CardioCorp

Alex — great speaking this morning. Quick recap and proposed path forward from our call: 

- Key ask: CardioCorp needs an evidence-first evaluation focused on PHI processing (HIPAA/BAA) and SOC 2 Type II controls before finalizing hosting mode. You flagged two blockers: (1) internal legal needs a BAA template + timeline, (2) security wants a short-run of infra evidence for Dedicated vs Private VPC routing.

Proposed next steps (timeline in days):
1) I’ll share a 1-page SOC2 excerpt + BAA draft today (attached).
2) Run a focused evidence sprint (3 business days) to collect logs/config snippets and a deployment-runbook comparing Hosted / Dedicated / Private for your use-case. Marissa will lead the sprint from Redwood side.
3) CardioCorp to confirm whether procurement prefers a Dedicated reservation or a Private VPC pilot after seeing evidence; if neither, Hosted remains an option with mitigations we discussed (data segregation controls + contract addenda).

Can you confirm: (a) stakeholders for the evidence sprint (security contact / procurement rep), and (b) legal’s target sign-off date for a BAA?

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf (stub), BAA_Draft_CardioCorp.docx (stub)

Thanks — I’ll queue up the sprint plan once we have the attendee list.

— Sean G.
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardiocorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@cardiocorp.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T10:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit sprint proposal & hosting decision — CardioCorp

Thanks Sean — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Security owner: Priya Rao (cc’d). She’ll need the SOC 2 excerpt mapped to our control set (particularly around encryption in transit+rest, key management, and access logging).
- Legal: I’ll ask legal to review the BAA draft; target internal review by EOD Friday (2028-01-20).
- Sprint attendees: Priya (security), me (product), and I’ll loop in procurement if we go Dedicated/Private.

Couple of asks up-front: can you include an explicit list of the logs/artifacts Redwood will provide during the 3-day sprint (e.g., sample audit logs, access control lists, KV cache handling notes, network flow summaries)? Also—will the sprint require any CardioCorp test data or can Redwood provide anonymized examples?

If you can get the artifact checklist today, we’ll confirm participants and timing.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Director of Product Security | CardioCorp
alex.chen@cardiocorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardiocorp.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit sprint proposal & hosting decision — CardioCorp

Alex / Sean — looping in the sprint plan. Per Sean’s note, we’ll run a focused 3-business-day "Evidence Sprint" once you confirm attendees. Below is the minimal artifact checklist Redwood will produce and share as separate deliverables (PDF/zip stubs):

Sprint artifact checklist (deliverables from Redwood):
- SOC2 excerpt mapped: control -> evidence (logs/config location)
- Sample audit logs (authentication events, token issuance, admin actions) — redacted/example CSV
- Key management summary (KMS/HSM integration diagram + access policy excerpt)
- Network topology snapshot for Dedicated and Private VPC options (egress controls, peering, firewall rules)
- Deployment runbook: step-by-step for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (including data flow diagrams and rollback steps)
- Quantified SLA comparisons and expected latency/throughput for your baseline workload (simple perf matrix)

What we need from you prior to sprint kickoff:
- Confirm security + procurement attendees (names + emails)
- A short list of 3 sample API interactions/endpoints you care about most (so we tailor logs and perf matrix)
- Whether you can provide a small anonymized request set (preferred) or if Redwood should use synthetic examples

Proposed sprint window: Jan 24–26 (Mon–Wed). If CardioCorp prefers earlier, we can try Jan 22–24 but that shortens prep time.

I’ve attached the SOC2 summary and BAA draft to this thread — please mark redlines in the doc and return. We’ll prepare a redline-friendly DocuSign link after legal feedback.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Security Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cardiocorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@cardiocorp.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Audit sprint proposal & hosting decision — CardioCorp

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick confirmations: 

- Sprint attendees: Priya Rao (security), Alex Chen (product), Samir Patel (procurement — samir.patel@cardiocorp.com).
- API endpoints: /v1/patient/summary, /v1/notes/generate, /v1/embeddings/batch (we’ll provide sample payloads by EOD Tue).
- We prefer Redwood to use anonymized synthetic data for the sprint to avoid PII handling in the evaluation environment.

Sprint window Jan 24–26 works for us. Legal aims to return BAA redlines by Jan 20. Please send the DocuSign link for final execution once redlines are addressed.

One last ask: for the Dedicated vs Private comparison, could you include a short ride-along cost estimate (3 options: Hosted + mitigation, Dedicated 3-node reserved, Private VPC pilot) so procurement has an initial frame?

If you can confirm those items, we’ll lock the sprint.

— Alex
